endorsements.quote: Ubuntu's emphasis on shared responsibility and inclusive well‐being requires that AI systems be co‐designed with local communities, taking into account environmental constraints and being attentive to the voices of those who have been historically marginalized.
We propose engaging community advisory boards following the “Made in Africa AI” approach that prioritizes community‐driven, participatory methods and indigenous definitions of success [ 83 ].

There is a need to conduct bias audits using frameworks developed by initiatives like the African AI Ethics and Human Rights research project, which supports interdisciplinary research across seven African countries [ 84 ].
The feedback channels allow patients and providers to report misdiagnoses or usability issues directly, so that AI tools evolve responsively to the real conditions of African clinical practice.

For African healthcare, ethics committees should include patient advocates, nurses, and community health workers to ensure AI governance reflects the realities of those who directly deliver and receive care.
Training frontline healthcare workers, not just computer scientists, in the ethical use of AI empowers nurses, midwives, and physicians to integrate AI into patient care safely and confidently.

unlisted_practices: Curate and maintain open-source healthcare AI models fine-tuned with African clinical data.
Establish regional AI hubs hosting healthcare AI models on low-cost servers with offline compatibility.
Partner with governments and telecom providers to subsidize compute resources and connectivity for rural clinics and district hospitals.
Establish pan-African AI consortia to pool scarce clinical data, coordinate disease surveillance, and share AI solutions.
Invest in building local capacity for healthcare AI development, including young entrepreneurs, developers, policymakers, and healthcare workers.
Prioritize lightweight model architectures such as quantization and pruning to reduce AI energy consumption.
Implement edge computing solutions that process data locally to reduce energy use.
Establish local AI stewards for maintenance and performance monitoring across the AI lifecycle.
Form regional multi-stakeholder ethics committees incorporating Ubuntu principles to oversee healthcare AI.
Place the burden of proof on AI proponents to demonstrate that AI development will not harm people or the environment (precautionary principle).
Assess whether AI is the most effective response to healthcare needs compared with investments in workforce and infrastructure.

screen.reason: This paper presents a conceptual and ethical framework (Ubuntu philosophy) to guide justice, solidarity, and sustainability in the governance and deployment of AI in African healthcare.
